Horowitz Senior Music Writer speriod Latest Paul McCartney Becomes a Billionaire, Making Him the World’s Third-Richest Musician 1 hour ago Katseye Postpones Chicago and Minneapolis Shows Due to Megan’s Illness 4 days ago Trent Reznor and Atticus Ross to Score David Fincher’s ‘The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth’ 7 days ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Kurt Iswarienko Pink has announced that she will be staging a residency at Las Vegas’ Sphere in 2027, making her the first solo female pop artist to headline the venue. The pop singer is slated to perform a string of dates next fall. Dates for the residency are September 29, October 1, October 2, October 6, October 8, October 9, October 27, October 29 and October 30. In a post on social media, Pink shared that the show has been in the works for quite some time. “Makes me think of celebration. Makes me feel like I’m on top of the world,” she wrote. “This idea has been bubbling up for years. And I finally get to share it with all of you! Let’s celebrate! The highs, the lows, the new, the scary, the never been done before. For the first time, I’m giving a show a home and I hope you’ll visit. It’s my FIRST EVER residency. @spherevegas, 2027. I can’t wait to have you over. 🩷” Related Stories Hulu’s ‘The Circle’ Revival Sets SiriusXM’s Tinx as Host (EXCLUSIVE) View this post on Instagram Artist presale registration is currently available on Pink’s website . Presale begins on November 18 at 10 a.m. PT, while Vibee package presale starts November 11 at 10 a.m. PT. General onsale starts November 20 at 10 a.m. PT. To coincide with the Sphere residency, the SlotZilla zipline at Fremont Street Experience will be rebranded as “P!nkzilla” for a limited aerial attraction. It will run from November 11 through November 19. Pink most recently staged her “Summer Carnival” tour across 2023 and 2024, followed by her “Trustfall” tour in 2023 and 2024. She was nominated for the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame earlier this year, joining a spate of artists including Mariah Carey, Lauryn Hill, Oasis, Shakira and Luther Vandross. This past June, she headed to Broadway to host the 79th Tony Awards. More recently, Pink made headlines after facing backlash for reposting a call for Macklemore to be dropped from the Ed Sheeran tour in the wake of his nightly pro-Palestinian songs and statements. She swiftly made her perspective clear, posting a long message about the controversy. “To the ones who are furious with me: you don’t have to agree with me,” she wrote. “You never did. That’s been our unspoken agreement for twenty-five years, and it still stands, and so do I. You don’t have to agree with one thing Israel’s government does to not want the Jewish family two rows down from you to be scared or targeted at a concert. That’s the only thing I’m asking anybody for. To the ones who are frightened this week, Jewish or Muslim or Palestinian or Israeli or just tired of all of it: I see you. And if anybody wants to really know what I think, just ask me. I’m right here. I’ve never been hard to find. And I’ll keep speaking out, in my own words.” Nate Bargatze Returns to Netflix With New Special ‘Good for Nathan’ (EXCLUSIVE) Loading comments...

title: John Turturro on Choosing Christopher Walken as His ‘Severance’ Love Interest and Auditioning to Play Madonna’s Boyfriend: ‘She Really Kissed Me’
full_text: Nov 9, 2026 9:15am PT John Turturro on Choosing Christopher Walken as His ‘Severance’ Love Interest and Auditioning to Play Madonna’s Boyfriend: ‘She Really Kissed Me’ By Isabelle Farina Plus Icon Isabelle Farina Latest John Turturro on Choosing Christopher Walken as His ‘Severance’ Love Interest and Auditioning to Play Madonna’s Boyfriend: ‘She Really Kissed Me’ 2 hours ago Tate McRae and Doechii Choreographer Robbie Blue Among World Choreography Award Winners 12 hours ago ‘I’ve Had It’ Podcast Hosts Jennifer Welch and Angie Sullivan Apologize for Laughing at Charlie Kirk Joke: ‘We Regret It’ 23 hours ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source With over 120 acting credits to his name, John Turturro has accrued a long list of what-ifs and missed opportunities, including a role as Madonna’s boyfriend. Turturro joined Variety’s co-editor in chief Ramin Setoodeh to chat in partnership with the Miami Film Festival and receive the Creative Vanguard Award. In this conversation, the seasoned actor recalled his memorable audition with the pop star in her early days for the 1985 comedic “Desperately Seeking Susan.” Related Stories Hulu’s ‘The Circle’ Revival Sets SiriusXM’s Tinx as Host (EXCLUSIVE) “I auditioned for Madonna’s boyfriend. I didn’t know who Madonna was,” Turturro said. “She wasn’t that famous, and we had a kissing scene and she really kissed me. I mean, deeply. I was like, ‘I’ve never been kissed like that in an audition.’ I dropped all my sides, all my pages on the floor. I was like, ‘I thought this was an audition. I didn’t know it was this kind of movie.’” Ultimately, he didn’t get the role as her fictional boyfriend — he played the comical club manager Ray instead — but he claimed her interest in him lasted long after their audition, but he preferred they stick to being friends. “Because some people, you feel like maybe they want to absorb you and I didn’t want to be absorbed,” Turturro said. “I do like her; we’ve always gotten along, but because we didn’t get absorbed. I haven’t seen her in a long time because she was married to all these different guys. I’m married to one woman. One wife is enough. That’s my motto.” Turturro’s extensive filmography means he has stories like this with some of the biggest names in Hollywood, including Martin Scorsese, Tom Cruise, Spike Lee, the Coen brothers, Adam Sandler, Zoë Kravitz and Meryl Streep, to name a few. Along with his slew of interesting stories, his vast career has granted him the freedom to choose which roles he agrees to and which he declines. For Turturro, big-budget franchises versus indie films or plays are two kinds of jobs that fulfill different needs: one gives him financial stability, the other gives him the opportunity to grow as an actor. “[Franchises are] my electrical job, and my other kind of job is my plumbing job, so I consider myself a plumber and then I do some electrical work,” Turturro said. He also revealed he was trusted with the decision of who would play his love interest in Apple TV’s hit series “Severance.” He chose longtime friend Christopher Walken. “He’s actually underestimated,” Turturro said of Walken playing his romantic interest on the show. “People don’t realize the different things he can do. He has a vulnerability to him and a delicacy that people sometimes think is strange, but he’s actually a delicate person and that was the reason I did the show.” It was helpful for Turturro to have a comrade on set because COVID-19 made the Season 1 shooting conditions less than ideal. “With masks and shields, and in that office, it was easy to have a nervous breakdown in that place,” Turturro said. “I was like, ‘I got to get out of this place if it was the last thing I had to do.’” While he is keeping his character Irving’s future in “Severance” under wraps, the actor was eager to discuss his latest starring role as Harry in “The Only Living Pickpocket in New York,” especially the film’s “beautiful” script. “It had a radical gentleness, and so many things nowadays are just in your face,” Turturro said. “The news is in your face, sports are in your face, movies are in your face. I felt there was a humanity to the world, and also there’s an element of class in it that people are struggling to live. That’s what makes an interesting character: obstacles.” Turturro’s portrayal of the complex character has begun to generate Oscar buzz for him — a nomination he has yet to receive in his decades-spanning career. But awards are not at the front of his mind when choosing which projects to participate in. “This is a crazy lifestyle,” Turturro said. “Time becomes more precious as I get older. So, I want to know if I’m going to do something, what am I going to do? And is it something I want to do? And I don’t want to repeat myself. I want to add to whatever I created. I’m not interested in doing the same, singing the same song. Sometimes some singers have to always sing that hit song.” Nate Bargatze Returns to Netflix With New Special ‘Good for Nathan’ (EXCLUSIVE) Loading comments...

title: Paramount+ Names Damla Dogan As Unscripted Chief
full_text: Skip to main content By Peter White Peter White Executive Editor, Television @peterzwhite More Stories By Peter ‘Call Her Daddy’s Alex Cooper Officially Moves To CAA After Leaving UTA ‘The Terminal List’ Franchise Continues At Amazon With ‘Savage Son’ Danielle Steel’s ‘The Whittiers’ In The Works As Series From Cottage Industry Entertainment & Fox Entertainment Studios View All October 30, 2026 9:45am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Story Arc Damla Dogan Paramount EXCLUSIVE : Paramount+ officially has a new unscripted boss. The streamer has named Damla Dogan as head of unscripted, overseeing reality programming. It caps off a busy couple of weeks on the executive front for parent company Skydance . The move comes after Casey Bloys, Co-Chair and Chief Content Officer, Skydance DTC, who will oversee content for both HBO Max and Paramount+, revealed his leadership team last week. Related Stories Executives Casey Bloys Unveils His Skydance DTC Content Team Featuring All HBO Max Execs: Francesca Orsi, Sarah Aubrey, Amy Gravitt & More Executives Paramount+ Brings In Former Netflix Exec Damla Dogan To Aid Unscripted Development Sarah Aubrey was named Head of Paramount+, Max Originals and International Programming and Dogan will report to her. Watch on Deadline Former Netflix exec Dogan has been consulting for Paramount+ for the last nine months, as first revealed by Deadline . She has already been busy, working closely with Jane Wiseman, who was previously EVP and Head of Originals for Paramount+, buying projects such as Making Love, a dating show from Kinetic Content, and Team Moms, the Kim Kardashian-exec produced youth baseball series from ITV America and Skydance Sports that launched last month. The move has been welcomed by the unscripted community, which has been buoyed by another buyer in the market – Paramount+ rarely bought original unscripted projects, outside of its own IP, before David Ellison’s Skydance took over. Before joining Paramount+, Dogan spent six years at Netflix, where she was Director of Unscripted Originals. She worked on series including Owning Manhattan, The Circle, Bling Empire, Buying Beverly Hills, Indian Matchmaking and Get Organized with The Home Edit. Prior to Netflix, she spent 11 years at E! Entertainment, where she developed Keeping Up With The Kardashians , which she oversaw for the first 14 seasons, as well as Total Divas and Love From The Red Carpet. full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News DC Studios Shakeup: James Gunn & Peter Safran Out, Former Marvel Exec Jeremy Latcham In Read the full story By Nellie Andreeva Nellie Andreeva Editor-In-Chief @DeadlineNellie More Stories By Nellie Druski Leads One Of ‘SNL’s Most Star-Studded Curtain Calls Ever With Emma Stone, Michael B. Jordan, Austin Butler, Plus Chappelle, Rock, Goggins ‘Heated Rivalry’ Hat Trick: Hit Series Filming Season 2, Season 3 And A Movie – The Dish ‘Grey’s Anatomy’ Spinoff Pushed To 2027-28, Moves Production To New Mexico After Failing To Get CA Tax Credit As Betsy Beers Calls For Program Change View All November 3, 2026 5:12pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Story Arc Francesca Orsi and Sarah Aubrey Courtesy Almost a month into Paramount’s acquisition of Warner Bros Discovery into Skydance, pieces are still coming together, and there is probably no area with more pieces to sort out than Skydance’s Direct to Consumer. With the content operations of Paramount+ and HBO/ HBO Max combined under Casey Bloys , now Co-Chair and Chief Content Officer, Skydance DTC, the former HBO & HBO Content CEO saw his portfolio more than double overnight. The expansion is passed on to his senior team which he brought over from HBO/HBO Max, led by Francesca Orsi , Amy Gravitt and Sarah Aubrey , with Paramount+’s EVP and Head of Originals Jane Wiseman leaving as part of the restructuring announced October 23 . Watch on Deadline Related Stories Executives Casey Bloys Unveils His Skydance DTC Content Team Featuring All HBO Max Execs: Francesca Orsi, Sarah Aubrey, Amy Gravitt & More News New Skydance Sets Top Executive Structure As Paramount-WBD Merger Set To Close Organizing the combined slate has been a priority for the new regime as it is reviewing Paramount+’s development and production pipeline. The process is in early stages and sources stress that no decisions have been made, but various ideas are being discussed, including possibly relocating upcoming Paramount+ drama series to HBO, I hear. Logical targets for a move to HBO are legal thriller Discretion , starring Big Little Lies ‘ Nicole Kidman and Elle Fanning, which has frequently been described as HBO-like; 9/11 first responders limited series The Best of Us , which is headlined by Emmy-winning Succession star Jeremy Strong; as well as a couple of projects awaiting official green light. There have been conversations, which I hear have reached the highest levels, but no migrations, with all series earmarked for Paramount+ remaining there for the time being. Talks are continuing. Even if the two streamers’ slates remain status quo — they are bound to merge eventually as Skydance co-CEO David Ellison has revealed plans for HBO Max and Paramount+ to become one platform in the next couple of years — there could be an HBO stamp on some upcoming Paramount+ dramas via potential involvement by Orsi. While Paramount+ has been staying largely out of the original comedy series game, BET+’s The Varnell Hill Show being a rare exception, its original drama slate is extensive, led by the flagship Taylor Sheridan universe. (The streamer also has next-day comedies and drama procedurals coming from CBS.) In the new structure, HBO Max’s Head of Originals Aubrey, now Head of Paramount+, Max Originals and International Programming, added oversight of all Paramount+ programming, with Wiseman’s team reporting to her. As part of the same realignment, Orsi was promoted from EVP to President, HBO Drama Series and Films in an expanded new role that involves her working with Bloys on determining which drama projects are best suited for HBO. I hear that may involve her taking oversight of Paramount+ original dramas that carry HBO DNA, whether they relocate to HBO or not. Aubrey and Orsi are currently reviewing the Paramount+ drama slate together, and I hear there is a possibility for Orsi to work on shows that stay on Paramount+ whenever it makes sense. title: Skydance Distribution Chief Ray Hopkins Sets Leadership Team, Reveals Exits Of Eight Senior…
full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News DC Studios Shakeup: James Gunn & Peter Safran Out, Former Marvel Exec Jeremy Latcham In Read the full story By Dade Hayes Dade Hayes Business Editor @dadehayes More Stories By Dade AI-Focused Management Firm Collage Adds Kelly Miller And Jack Styne As Partners Tubi CEO Anjali Sud, Roku Media President Charlie Collier Leaving The Fold As Fox Sets Exec Team After Roku Close Charter Stock Sinks As Internet Subscriber Losses Worsen; Could A Comcast Merger Be The Next Move? View All November 4, 2026 2:57pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Story Arc Deadline In the latest in a series of organizational announcements following the closing of the Paramount-Warner Bros Discovery merger into Skydance , the newly combined company has set its top distribution troops. Ray Hopkins , the longtime CBS veteran who is now distribution president of Skydance , sent an internal memo Tuesday outlining the newly minted execs in his organization and also noting several departures. Related Stories News New Skydance Sets Top Executive Structure As Paramount-WBD Merger Set To Close Executives David Decker Lands Top Content Sales Role At Skydance With Jay Askinasi Overseeing Ads, Ray Hopkins Leading Distribution Distribution deals will be overseen jointly by Sarah Bergman and Mickey Carter, both of whom hold the title of EVP, Distribution. Bergman has been with HBO and WBD for 14 years, while Carter brings more than a decade of Paramount and CBS experience. Their portfolio spans CBS owned-and-operated stations, 55 basic cable networks, two premium networks, plus subscription streamers Paramount+, HBO Max and Discovery+; free streamer Pluto TV; and more than 100 FAST channels. While distribution is a hugely important business area for all players in the media sector, it is particularly crucial for Skydance, which has almost $80 billion in debt following the $110 billion transaction. In order to reduce that leverage, the company will need to wring as much cash as possible from its partners, but it is also constrained by a consent decree established by state attorneys general in the resolution of an antitrust lawsuit. The agreement requires Skydance to negotiate carriage deals for the Paramount and WBD families of assets as though they were still run by separate companies. Watch on Deadline Hopkins said eight execs will be exiting Skydance as part of the new appointments: WBD’s Rivka Golomb, Kelly Kane, Jeff Cross and Rich Palermo, and Paramount vets David Comisar, Kurt Davis, Deena Demasi and Ken Kay. Other executive appointments include the following: Brad Shipley, EVP, Business Development & Strategy . Shipley, who joined CBS 13 years ago, will oversee strategy, new growth partnerships, Pluto TV and FAST distribution, advanced advertising partnerships as well as business planning and analytics and also be distribution lead for Skydance Global Sports Group. Patrick Cavanaugh, EVP & CFO, Distribution Finance . Following nearly 14 years at the YES Network, he has spent the last decade at CBS and Paramount. He will lead economics for all linear and streaming negotiations, manage the linear affiliate revenue life cycle from deal negotiation through cash collection, as well as all budgeting, forecasting and reporting. Rick Baker, EVP, Deputy General Counsel, Distribution, Business & Legal Affairs . Baker, who joined MTV Networks in 2011, will oversee business and legal affairs for Skydance’s distribution across linear and streaming including domestic broadcast, premium and cable networks, P+, HBO Max, Discovery +, Pluto TV and FAST. With the new role, Cross, EVP, Legal, Distribution & Commercial Partnerships, will be leaving the organization but will remain a senior advisor to the distribution group. Joe Bahr, SVP, Partner Operations . With more than 20 years across HBO, WarnerMedia and WBD, Bahr will manage operational issues across partners, serve as the liaison to product and tech teams, and support delivery of linear and VOD offerings to distributors. Andrew Borak, SVP, Marketing . After starting in affiliate marketing at MTV 20 years ago, Borak has been SVP, Distribution Marketing for Paramount for the past six years. He will lead the combined distribution marketing function, market to distributors and with distributors, lead cross-brand distribution initiatives, and prepare marketing strategies for distribution renewals. Bob Aguanno, SVP, CBS Affiliate Relations . The 25-plus-year CBS veteran will manage relationships with roughly 200 CBS affiliate TV stations and work closely with the CBS Network affiliate board. John Bagwell, SVP, Associate General Counsel . Bagwell has served for more than a decade as lead counsel for CBS Network distribution via the CBS affiliated stations and will negotiate contracts with the station groups and the CBS Network affiliate board. title: DC Studios Shakeup: James Gunn & Peter Safran Out, Former Marvel Exec Jeremy Latcham In
full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News DC Studios Shakeup: James Gunn & Peter Safran Out, Former Marvel Exec Jeremy Latcham In Read the full story By Anthony D'Alessandro Anthony D'Alessandro Editorial Director/Box Office Editor @AwardsTony More Stories By Anthony ‘Godzilla Minus Zero’ Is A Box Office Hero With $32M Live-Action Foreign-Language Opening Record, Best Ever For Gkids – Sunday AM Update ‘Godzilla Minus Zero’ Is King Of The Global Weekend Box Office With $63M, Towers Over ‘Ramayana’s $55M+ WW Opening ‘Hunger Games: Sunrise On The Reaping’ Getting Hot With $80M+ Opening Floor, Presales Ahead Of ‘Wicked’ – Box Office Update View All November 9, 2026 9:16am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Story Arc James Gunn and Peter-Safran; Jeremy Latcham Getty/John Winters In a seismic executive shuffle unlike anything Bruce Wayne could pull off at Wayne Enterprises, James Gunn and Peter Safran are leaving their posts as Co-CEOs and Chairman of DC Studios , jobs which they’ve held for the past four years. The dynamic duo will continue to produce on various DC projects and returning to their full-time creative work. They’re currently in post on the Superman sequel, Man of Tomorrow which will open in theaters on July 9, 2027. Related Stories News James Gunn Is Writing His Next Movie Following ‘Man of Tomorrow’: “Already In It” Executives Josh Greenstein & Dana Goldberg Poised To Run Combined Paramount Warner Bros Film Unit Taking over the comic book entertainment label as President and Chief Creative Officer is former Marvel SVP of Production and Development, Jeremy Latcham . He starts the position on Dec. 1 and reports to Skydance Motion Picture Group co-chairs, Dana Goldberg and Josh Greenstein. Duly note the tweak here in the reporting structure of DC: Initially the DC Bosses reported straight into the CEO (previously Zaslav, post-merger David Ellison and Ynon Kreiz. Now DC like the other Warner film labels reports into Goldberg and Greenstein. Latcham worked with Gunn previously on Guardians of the Galaxy. Latcham shepherded such mega MCU franchises as Iron Man, Guardians of the Galaxy, Spider-Man and The Avengers . He will lead DC’s film, television and animation slate, overseeing the creative pipeline, along with production, talent and strategy. Watch on Deadline The news hits today as DC’s new parent, Skydance, is reporting their third quarter earnings. For some, the dynamic duo’s departure is a bit of a shock as sources told us that they were staying post Paramount’s acquisition of Warner Bros. However, word was out there that Safran’s contract was expiring in the spring. His name was floated for the film boss job at Netflix under newly installed Film Content Chief Peter Rice, however, from what we know, Safran and Rice haven’t sat down. Gunn and Safran were put in charge of DC by former Warner Bros Discovery CEO David Zaslav as he strove to create a motion picture production label strategy on par with Disney’s. The hiring of Gunn in a creative production executive position was arguably an anomaly: Few filmmakers have led studios; Charlie Chaplin being one of the most notable ones. Gunn and Safran took over DC at a time when the label was waning under the Zack Snyder universe. Zaslav wanted a universe that was built out across film, TV and games. The former WBD boss was adamant about making a Superman movie, and former WB Motion Pictures bosses quietly contracted Gunn to start writing his version before he landed the job with Conjuring producer Safran. During their tenure, they saw the airing of the Matt Reeves’ produced 9x Emmy-winning HBO Max series, The Penguin, a spinoff of the filmmaker’s The Batman starring Colin Farrell. That series was well in the works before Gunn and Safran arrived at DC. They also had two seasons of the Emmy-nominated HBO Max series Peacemaker, which was a spinoff of Gunn’s 2021 Suicide Squad movie starring that pic’s anti-hero played by John Cena. Let’s not forget the animated HBO adult series Creature Commandos. Gunn’s Superman rebooted the franchise a fourth time since the Man of Steel hit the big screen in 1978 with a $618.7M global gross. Their HBO Max series, Lanterns, was a viewership success and their lower budget Clayface with a net $44M production cost was No. 1 worldwide for two weeks in a row, that James Watkins-directed pic’s cume now at $109M WW. Upcoming is Reeves’ The Batman II which has Robert Pattinson returning in the title role and Steven Soderbergh finishing in London for a Feb. 18, 2028 release. Also upcoming for DC in 2027 is The People v. Gorilla Grodd , the eight-episode HBO Max series starring Skyler Gisondo as Jimmy Olsen and Jimmy Tatro as Gorilla Grodd has completed filming. Gunn and Safran serve as executive producers. A big miss for Gunn and Safran was the Craig Gillespie directed Supergirl which cost a net $186M and grossed only $126.4M WW. A graphic novel which was True Grit in its story, the Superman spinoff arrived a year after Gun’s Man of Steel movie, and was perceived by fanboys as being too similar to other fantasy movies, i.e. Mad Max and Guardians of the Galaxy. Gunn and Safran had a big plan for DC, announced as “Gods and Monsters” in January 2023 . It will be interesting to see what projects Goldberg, Greenstein and Latcham keep intact. There was early buzz of James Mangold circling a Swamp Thing movie, and Andy Muscietti penning a version of Batman Brave and the Bold . Of the projects Gunn and Safran announced which wound up fizzling after being long in development was the Peacemaker spinoff series Waller starring Viola Davis, Paradise Lost a series set in the Wonder Woman -verse, Booster Gold and an Authority movie about a bunch of DC antiheroes. Gunn said in February 2025 on social that Authority “is a very big movie, if you’re going to do it properly. Some of the story elements perhaps that are in Superman and some of the other films we fast-tracked, step a little on The Authority … [It’s] the one that got messed with through all of the other things that were happening. The script had a harder time coming along.” In fact, Gunn announced recently he was working on a screenplay for a new feature project . What’s the status of that mystery project? It’s been a while since Latcham has been in the superhero space. He left the Kevin Feige led Marvel in 2017 to found Latcham Pictures, which held first-look deals at 20th Century Fox, Hasbro, and Wonder Project. He produced Bad Times at the El Royale and Dungeons & Dragons: Honor Among Thieves . Recently, he held an overall deal at Hasbro Entertainment, where he was developing a Dungeons & Dragons sequel and an Action Man film. He’s also producing Lionsgate and Sony’s big screen take of anime Naruto which has Spider-Man: Brand New Day ‘s Destin Daniel Cretton directing. David Ellison, Chairman and CEO, and Ynon Kreiz, Co-CEO, of Skydance said in a statement about today’s news, “James and Peter launched a new era for DC Studios and led it through a period of real transformation, resetting the foundation and building a slate we’re incredibly proud of. We’re grateful for their passion, contributions and commitment to this legendary brand. Jeremy has been a longtime creative partner to both, and we have complete confidence that James and Peter will ensure a smooth, collaborative transition and continue this work with care. We look forward to working with Jeremy to build the next generation of DC storytelling and to doubling down on our commitment to fans.” Said Gunn and Safran: “Four years ago, we set out to unite DC under one creative vision. In that time, we helped restore Superman to the heart of DC, while opening new doors and telling new stories in film and television with Peacemaker , Creature Commandos, Lanterns and Clayface. We’re immensely proud of the team that turned that ambition into something real, including the actors, crews and executives we had the opportunity to collaborate with. We’ve shared a creative history with Jeremy going back to Marvel, and we’re eager to see the perspective he brings to DC’s next chapter. We’re excited to return to what drew us to this job in the first place, which is telling the stories we love, including the next chapter of Clark and Lex’s journey in Man of Tomorrow .” Gunn also posted the following to IG: View this post on Instagram “Jeremy brings a deep reverence for DC and its passionate fanbase, recognizing that they are the very foundation of this storied, multigenerational brand,” said Goldberg and Greenstein. “Under his leadership, every film and television show will be ushered from start to finish through the prism of the legions of fans who love and champion it. Jeremy’s track record exemplifies the excellence he will bring to building out DC and the many beloved characters within it.” “DC’s pantheon of characters is among the most iconic in American popular culture. I’ve had the privilege to help bring some of the most celebrated superhero stories to life on the big screen, and I’m excited and honored for the opportunity to now lead DC Studios into its next era. The chance to steward the incredible cast of DC characters to the screen in a way that excites lifelong fans while introducing their timeless stories to the next generation is a massive responsibility that I do not take lightly,” said Latcham. “I am grateful to Dana and Josh for putting their trust in me. I can’t wait to work night and day alongside filmmakers, comic book creators, artists and storytellers of every kind, across film, television and animation, to build something ambitious for longtime DC fans and newcomers alike.” ‘Yellowstone’s Cole Hauser Preps FBI Action Thriller ‘Pale Horse’ With Eye To Star ‘Godzilla’ Stalks $32M U.S. Bow, Best For Live-Action Foreign-Language Pic 10½-Year Prison Sentence; Survivor Speaks Out, Rips Channel 4 De Niro Targets Elon At ‘Musk’ Documentary Screening On GOP Spending Spree More from this Story Arc Skydance November 4, 2026 Skydance Distribution Chief Ray Hopkins Sets Leadership Team, Reveals Exits Of Eight Senior Executives November 3, 2026 Paramount+ Drama Slate: Series Moving To HBO, Sarah Aubrey & Francesca Orsi Sharing Oversight Among Options Explored Post-Merger – The Dish View All Story Arc Read More About: 43 Comments
